newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigerian court postpones decision on Abiola lawyer.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian court postpones decision on Abiola lawyer.

text.p: A Nigerian appeal court on Thursday postponed a decision on whether detained opposition leader Moshood Abiola should appear in court to name his lawyer for his treason trial.

Two Nigerian lawyers have been feuding for months over which of them should represent Abiola in his treason trial in a separate court that has stalled since August 1994 when he was last seen in public.
Abiola has been detained since 1994 when he defied the military government and proclaimed himself president based on the results of an annulled 1993 presidential election.

"We maintain that there is no need for Chief Abiola to appear in court to announce his legal counsel because there are other ways he can clarify this such as swearing an affidavit," government lawyer Tochukwu Nwabufor told the Abuja court.
But Rotimi Williams, who this year announced he was Abiola's new lawyer, said the politician should come to court to name his counsel since it was not possible to contact him directly.
Judge Umaru Kalgo, sitting with two other justices, said the appeal court would fix a date to rule on the submissions and notify all the parties involved.
Abiola's family is divided over whether Williams, Nigeria's most prominent lawyer, should take over his defence or his original lawyer Godwin Ajayi should continue to handle the case.

According to Abiola's eldest son, his father asked him to brief Williams to handle the case while Abiola's senior wife Kudirat maintained up to when she was killed in June by unknown gunmen that there was no instruction to change counsel.
Abiola, one of Africa's richest men, is held in a secret location in Abuja and is rarely allowed visitors.
His family doctor, Ore Falomo, said on Thursday that he last saw Abiola two months ago.
"That was the last time I attended to his medical needs and I am sure that his health must now be worse because of his high blood pressure," Falomo told reporters at the court building.
